clue.text: Convoluted "non-U" jury testimonial leads to most of us passively agreeing

indicators.note: something convoluted is twisted and tangled, so the letters that remain are twisted into a new order
read literally, non-U means without U, so the letter U is removed from the words that follow

explanation.surface: A tortuous jury statement, criticised as not upper-class, is blamed for leaving most people meekly going along with things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-U' in Britain means not upper-class, but here it simply says 'no U': drop the U from JURY TESTIMONIAL and rearrange the remaining fourteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the large mass of ordinary people who do not voice opinions but tacitly go along with things.

clue.text: For Leslie, perhaps, more Dirty Den? That is right

definitions.note: Leslie stands for any Scot, and in Scots the comparative of a word for muddy means more dirty

parts.note: a lair is an animal's den
IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: An EastEnders query: was Leslie Grantham's character Dirty Den even more of a lout? That is right.
explanation.walkthrough: Leslie Grantham played Dirty Den in the British soap EastEnders, but Leslie here is just a typical Scottish name: in Scots, lairy means muddy, so the comparative means more dirty.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scots adjective describes ground or boots covered in mire, so its comparative suits a Scotsman's grubbier.

clue.text: Bill Bailey's fifth after missing tango

indicators.note: after puts the picked letter behind the other pieces

parts.note: no can mean lacking, as in 'no money'
T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: fifth points to the letter in fifth position of the following name

parts.note: the fifth letter of Bailey is E

explanation.surface: A puzzle about comedian Bill Bailey's fifth something, once the tango has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill Bailey' reads as the comedian, but Bill is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A banknote is a bill in American usage, and a note is also a short invoice or account.

clue.text: Security concern when touring Australia and America's monuments

indicators.note: touring suggests going all the way round, so the spy's word surrounds the next letters

parts.note: a mole, an infiltrated spy, is a worry for security services
A is an abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: A security worry arises as tourists visit Australian and American memorials.
explanation.walkthrough: A mole is a spy planted inside an organisation, hence a concern for security staff.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin plural of the word for a grand tomb building names stately funerary monuments.

clue.text: Pad top of jacket with fur

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of jacket is J
otter is a fur, the pelt of the otter

explanation.surface: Someone pads the collar of a jacket with fur trim.
explanation.definitionFit: A jotter is a small notebook, the kind of writing pad used for quick notes.

clue.text: Rising, repeat frequently after minister: "It's a raw deal for consumers"

definitions.text: It's a raw deal for consumers

indicators.note: after places the reversed letters behind the minister

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious minister

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: do, short for ditto, means repeat
oft is an old word for often

explanation.surface: A minister's repeated slogan protests that customers are getting an unfair bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raw deal' looks like unfairness, but it means uncooked food dealt out to eaters; DO, short for ditto, is the repeat sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabbit food is a jokey name for salad and raw vegetables, offered to eaters as something to eat.

clue.text: Piggy snaffles wine and snack

indicators.note: to snaffle is to grab, so the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: 'this little piggy' is the nursery rhyme counted on toes
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: A greedy pig grabs some wine and a bite to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme 'This little piggy', each piggy is a toe.
explanation.definitionFit: A toastie is a toasted sandwich, a popular quick bite in Britain.

clue.text: Peachtree St High "best in class" (perhaps unfairly)

indicators.note: high means intoxicated, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: An Atlanta high school on Peachtree Street boasts of a top pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: Peachtree Street is the main thoroughfare of Atlanta, Georgia; 'High' looks like a school, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The favourite pupil of the teacher may be rated the best in the class, whether deservedly or not.

clue.text: Be wary of cloud with colour that's reddish

parts.note: mist is a low cloud of fine droplets
rust is a reddish-brown colour

explanation.surface: Someone warns against a cloud tinged with a red hue, perhaps as a weather omen.
explanation.definitionFit: To distrust or be suspicious of something is to be wary of it, as a verb.

clue.text: Screeching from Red Robbo's employers many years back

parts.note: Red Robbo was Derek Robinson, militant union convenor at British Leyland, abbreviated BL

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for many years in the opposite direction

parts.note: an era is a long period of years

explanation.surface: A recollection of the racket from the car firm that employed a famous union militant decades ago.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Robbo was the nickname of Derek Robinson, a shop steward at British Leyland (BL), the British car maker, in the 1970s. ERA read backwards gives ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A blare is a loud harsh noise, so the noun matches a screeching sound.

clue.text: Videoconference on Cubist style portraying us as beastly

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the first piece sits on top

parts.note: Zoom is a videoconferencing platform
Orphism was an offshoot of Cubism led by Robert Delaunay

explanation.surface: An online meeting discusses a Cubist painting style.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoomorphism is depicting humans or gods with animal forms or attributes.

clue.text: One worshipped in silence?

parts.note: split as O and DIN, the answer reads as zero noise, which is what silence is

explanation.surface: A question about a god revered in quiet devotion.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer one and three: O (nothing) plus DIN (noise) means no noise at all, which is silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin is the chief god of Norse mythology, worshipped by the Vikings.

clue.text: Dickensian possibly forced evictions around middle of Chelsea

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the next piece
forced suggests pushed out of shape, so the letters of evictions are rearranged
middle of picks the central letter of the seven-letter word Chelsea

explanation.surface: Evictions forced through in central Chelsea sound like something from a Dickens novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Chelsea is a district of London; 'Dickensian' looks like grim social conditions, but it is one example of fiction-writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing in a Dickensian manner is one example of a style typical of fiction books.

clue.text: Horny African's garbled threats when ringing buzzer

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the mixed letters go round the insect
garbled means scrambled, so the letters of threats are mixed up

parts.note: a bee is a buzzing insect

explanation.surface: An African's muddled threats on the phone as the doorbell rings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horny' means having horns, not lustful, and 'buzzer' looks like a doorbell but is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The hartebeest is a large African antelope with distinctive curved horns.

clue.text: Two boys, both too short for girl

indicators.note: both names are cut short, each losing its final letter

parts.note: Mark and Gareth are two boys' names

explanation.surface: Two lads, both judged too small, are passed over in favour of a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: MARK loses its K and GARETH its H, and the two shortened names run together.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret is a female first name, so it is one example of a girl's name.

clue.text: After extremists defect, Socialist party is pretty useless

indicators.note: when the extremists, the outer letters, desert the word, only its inner letters stay

parts.note: a socialist is on the political left
a fete is an outdoor party or fair

explanation.surface: Once the hardliners desert, the Socialist party is left almost powerless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Socialist party' looks like one political body; Socialist gives a word for the political wing, which loses its two outer letters, then a word for a summer party follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Effete means feeble and ineffectual, lacking vigour, so near enough useless.

clue.text: Is Italy supporting bishop outside one of its ports?

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed below the earlier pieces

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
rind is the outer skin
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A question whether Italy backs a bishop beyond one of its harbours.
explanation.definitionFit: Brindisi is a seaport on the Adriatic coast in Apulia, southern Italy.

clue.text: Name pulled up is screened by network

indicators.note: being screened by something means being hidden inside it

parts.note: a rete is an anatomical network of blood vessels or nerves
PU is the horse-racing form abbreviation for pulled up

explanation.surface: Someone's name is withdrawn and then hidden by a broadcaster.
explanation.walkthrough: In racing form, PU marks a horse that was pulled up by its jockey; RETE is a network in anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Repute is reputation, as when someone has a good name in their community.

clue.text: Attitude after you are, in text message, butt of joke

parts.note: post means after, as in post-war
UR is text-speak for you are

indicators.note: the butt is the end, so the last letter of joke

parts.note: the last letter of joke is E

explanation.surface: Someone says in a text that you are now the butt of the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Posture is a stance or attitude, both literal and figurative.

clue.text: Western European stocks zips with Chinese clasps

indicators.note: to stock is to hold, so the reversed word holds the other letters
in an across clue, westward means right to left, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a Serb is a European from Serbia
zip is American slang for nothing, and two zeros look like the letter O twice

explanation.surface: A shop note: a European retailer carries zips alongside Chinese fasteners.
explanation.walkthrough: SERB read westward gives BRES, which holds OO and CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Brooches are ornamental pins fastened onto clothing, a kind of decorative clasp.

clue.text: In toto 100, as reported by Pope Linus perhaps for the Vatican

indicators.text: as reported by Pope Linus perhaps
indicators.note: an early pope like Linus would have said C for 100, and a report is heard spoken

parts.note: in toto means wholly, and 100 is C in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Totals reported by an early pope on behalf of the papal state.
explanation.walkthrough: Linus was the second pope, a Roman who would have written 100 as the numeral C; said aloud, wholly C gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy See is the jurisdiction of the Pope as Bishop of Rome, governed from the Vatican.

clue.text: Control river pests

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
lice are parasitic pests

explanation.surface: An order to deal with pests along a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To police something is to regulate or keep it in order, as a verb.

clue.text: Food mess post-war railway operator has

parts.note: to make a hash of something is to make a mess of it
BR, British Rail, ran Britain's railways from 1948
to own is to have

explanation.surface: The meal served up by Britain's nationalised railway is a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: British Rail (BR) was the state railway company formed after the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Hash browns are fried grated potato cakes eaten as a breakfast dish.

clue.text: Fruit only's churned guts

indicators.note: the guts of the word, its inner letters, are churned so they swap places

parts.note: sole means only, with the 's as a link

explanation.surface: Only this fruit has stirred-up insides.
explanation.walkthrough: Only its inner letters OL change places, becoming LO between S and E.
explanation.definitionFit: The sloe is the small sour berry of the blackthorn, used for flavouring gin.

clue.text: Leader laughs, looking skywards

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking skywards means read from bottom to top

parts.note: hahs are laughs

explanation.surface: A ruler laughs while gazing up at the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shah was the monarch of Iran, so a ruler or head of state.

clue.text: Liberal not attending tribute gets panned?

indicators.note: someone not attending is absent, so that letter leaves the word

parts.note: a salute is a gesture of tribute or honour

explanation.surface: A tribute that the Liberal skipped gets slated by critics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panned' looks like harsh criticism; it is cooking quickly in a pan.
explanation.definitionFit: To sauté is to fry quickly in a shallow pan, so sautéed food has been pan-fried.

clue.text: Maybe Murdoch man's masculine Milliganesquery?

parts.note: Iris Murdoch was the Irish-born novelist
his means belonging to a man
M is the grammar abbreviation for masculine

explanation.surface: Is the media mogul's man indulging in Spike Milligan-style silliness?
explanation.walkthrough: Murdoch suggests the media owner, but it is the novelist Iris Murdoch. Spike Milligan, the comedian, was famously of Irish descent.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irishism is an expression or bull characteristic of Irish speech, like Milligan's comic phrases.

clue.text: Warm up wine after decapsulating? Cape paganism!

parts.note: to heat is to warm up

indicators.note: decapsulating here means taking off the cap, the first letter

parts.note: Rhenish is wine from the Rhine region
a ness is a headland or cape

explanation.surface: A winemaker warms a bottle after uncorking it and exclaims at the heathen indulgence.
explanation.walkthrough: RHENISH loses its cap R to give HENISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathenishness is the state of being heathen, which is to say non-Christian pagan belief.
